//Eagle: The event card hw_tgr_eagle spawns. It is one popup with one button; clicking it destroys exactly ONE allow-listed card (AffectedCardsWarpData) that is LOOSE on the current location's ground row, never one in a container, trap, hand or equipment slot (AppliesTo 5 = AllCardsInBase reads only the base slot line of the board the player is on; LookInInventories false keeps it out of inventories), and shows the vanilla cards-destroyed popup with CustomDestroyMessage. There is deliberately NO NoCardsAffectedMessage: ApplyExtraDurabilitiesChanges runs a second, after-spawning pass that skips every change of this shape, finds nothing destroyed and would show that message as a SECOND popup right after a successful take (measured in the live game 2026-09-29, T2.448 and T2.444), so a click with nothing left to take is silent. If the roll ever moves from hw_tgr_eagle to C# this card, its button and its text stay as they are. The allow-list is Documentation/Research/HarshWilds/raids.md section 2, vanilla cards by GUID hash: Carcass_HareCarcass, Carcass_PartridgeCarcass, Carcass_DuckCarcass, Carcass_SquirrelCarcass, SquirrelRaw, MouseRaw, FrogRaw, BirdMeatRaw, PartridgeTiedFemale, PartridgeTiedMale, Fish_Trout, Fish_Perch, Fish_Pike, Fish_Char, CrayfishRaw; then Sirus23's wildowl_carcass and wildowl_tied by UniqueID, which WarpResolver drops with one Info 'unresolved' line when Sirus23 is not installed. The same 17 sit as bait rows in hw_tgr_eagle; keep the two lists identical (Development_Tools/Tests/HarshWilds-Eagle.Tests.ps1 checks it). Danger to keep in mind: a list whose every entry failed to resolve would leave AffectedCards empty, and ExtraDurabilityChange.AppliesToAllCards reads an empty list as ALL cards; the vanilla GUIDs cannot fail that way short of a broken game data load.
